jeffery.kaynak: Arthur Jeffery, The Foreign Vocabulary of the Qur'ān (Baroda 1938; Brill yeniden basımı, yazıya geçirilmiş metin; Arapça yazılar yazı tipi bozuk olduğundan alınmadı)
jeffery.metin: ii, 16. To be profitable. A trading term which Barth, Etymol. Stud, 29 (but cf. Torrey, Commercial Theological Terms, p. 44), has equated with the Jewish . It seems more likely, however, to have come from the Eth. lucrari, lucrifacere,4 which is very commonly used and has many derivatives, e.g. U a business man; 7 gain; Y profit bearing, etc., which are among the commonest trading terms. It is thus probably a trade term that came to the Arabs from Abyssinia, or may be from S. Arabia (cf. Ryckmans, Noms propres, i, 196; Rossini, Glossarium, 236).
